```markdown
Copy and assets to get Stream #1 on the air. Focus: the foundations of sound, real music technique, and the craft of building instruments and effects. Tools stay loose. Tone: curious, technical, professional.

**The pitch is written to win clicks, on Loudon's call (2026-10-21).** The tagline, About, trailer and titles in §1–§4 speak to the viewer and promise the answer each video gives. ## 1. Channel identity

**Channel name**

Loud'n Live (handles and URLs: `loudonlive`)

**Tagline**

Understand sound by building it.

It names the subject (sound, not tools) and says what the viewer gets.

**Banner text (one short line, plus schedule)**

> Loud'n Live · Understand sound by building it
> New every [DAY] · [TIME] [TZ]

If you don't have a fixed schedule yet, drop the second line. Don't put a schedule up you can't keep.

---

## 2. About / Channel description

The first line is the one most people read, so it carries the whole pitch.

> Learn how sound really works by building the instruments that make it.
>
> I'm Loudon: musician, music-tech educator, [one specific, true credential]. Here I build synthesizers and effects from scratch, take apart the ideas inside them, and turn them into music. Every video answers a question you can hear: why a sound feels warm, why a filter sweep feels like motion, why a phrase lands.
>
> What's here:
> · Deep dives into how sound works
> · Builds: synths, effects and instruments, made in front of you, including the parts that break
> · Read The Manual: one product's whole manual, tested section by section
> · Music technique for electronic producers
> · Livestreams where you can ask questions while the work happens
>
> New [videos/streams] every [DAY]. If you've ever turned a knob and wondered why it does that, subscribe.
>
> One-on-one coaching: [link]

Short version (Twitch panels, social bios):

> Understand sound by building it. Synths, effects and music technique for electronic musicians. New every [DAY].

---

## 3. Channel trailer script (~45 sec)

It opens on a sound, not a greeting, because the first seconds decide whether anyone stays. The work-in-progress line is gone for the same reason.

> [Cold open, no talking: the Lissajous logo turning, its chord sounding underneath. Four seconds.]
>
> You're hearing the logo. Three tones, each a hair out of tune with the others. That slow wobble in the sound is the same drift you see in the shape. Pull them into tune…
>
> [the figure locks; the chord goes still]
>
> …and both freeze.
>
> I'm Loudon. On Loud'n Live we figure out how sound works by building the things that make it — synths, effects, instruments — and then we make music with them.
>
> Some videos go deep on one idea, like that one. Some are builds. Some read a product's whole manual and test every page. Some are live, so you can ask questions while it happens.
>
> If you've ever turned a knob and wondered why it does that, subscribe. That's the whole channel.

The logo's chord is the Daily Page proof `proofs/the-logo-heard.html` (2026-10-14). Listen to it before building the trailer on it. Length target: 45–60 seconds. One take with a few mistakes left in is still on-brand.

---

Titles and thumbnails move views; the About and trailer barely do. Put the hook first: a question the ear can check, or a claim the video proves, plus one plain keyword, short enough to fit on a phone screen. Series tags go after the hook (`… · Live build`, `… · Sound lab`).

Promise only what the video delivers.

**Three example titles**

1. The sound that rises forever, and how to build it
2. Why a piano is never quite in tune with itself
3. I built a wavetable synth shaped like a donut
```

- **The design floor:** `_ops/loudon-live/design-system/SKILL.md:28` says "No outcome promises in titles."

Until those change, the note at the top of the kit is what stops the next agent from "fixing" the titles back. Changing them is a canon decision, though, and your "do it anyway" covered the pitch, not the channel's editorial stance. Do you want those two lines changed too, or kept as they are with the kit as the one exception?

turns.answer:
The Concierge couldn't be summoned: a hook blocked the spawn ("Not available in this session"). So no elder is with us today, and nothing below has been written to the palace.

**One tension, said once.** The palace judges this channel by "how do you feel?", not "how many views?" ([[Hilaritas Generator]]). The Loudon Live design rules also say no hype and no promised outcomes. You asked for clicks, and it's your channel, so this draft goes for them. Nothing it promises is untrue, and it has no hype or emoji. At the end I list each place it breaks a house rule, so you can choose which ones to keep.

There's also a problem that has nothing to do with taste. The launch kit was written in May and the entry was updated in October, so they disagree. The kit's banner, "synths, effects, and DSP, built on stream," is the tools-first identity the entry has since dropped. It still says "Loudon Live" where the wordmark is now Loud'n Live, and it leaves out the Read The Manual series and coaching. The rewrite fixes all of that either way.

**Understand sound by building it.**

Banner: `Loud'n Live · Understand sound by building it · New every [DAY]`

## About (YouTube)

The first line is the one people actually see, so it carries the whole pitch.

> Learn how sound really works by building the instruments that make it.
>
> I'm Loudon: musician, music-tech educator, [one specific, true credential]. Here I build synthesizers and effects from scratch, take apart the ideas inside them, and turn them into music. Every video answers a question you can hear: why a sound feels warm, why a filter sweep feels like motion, why a phrase lands.
>
> What's here:
> · Deep dives into how sound works
> · Builds: synths, effects and instruments, made in front of you, including the parts that break
> · Read The Manual: one product's whole manual, tested section by section
> · Music technique for electronic producers
> · Livestreams where you can ask questions while the work happens
>
> New [videos/streams] every [DAY]. If you've ever turned a knob and wondered why it does that, subscribe.
>
> One-on-one coaching: [link]

Short version (bios, panels):

> Understand sound by building it. Synths, effects and music technique for electronic musicians. New every [DAY].

I left the credential as a blank on purpose. A specific credential gets more clicks than a vague one, and I won't guess yours.

## Trailer (~45 sec)

The old trailer opened with "Hi, I'm Loudon." This one opens on a sound, because the first few seconds decide whether anyone stays. The channel's own logo is the best hook it has.

> [Cold open, no talking: the Lissajous logo turning, its chord sounding underneath. Four seconds.]
>
> You're hearing the logo. Three tones, each a hair out of tune with the others. That slow wobble in the sound is the same drift you see in the shape. Pull them into tune…
>
> [the figure locks; the chord goes still]
>
> …and both freeze.
>
> I'm Loudon. On Loud'n Live we figure out how sound works by building the things that make it — synths, effects, instruments — and then we make music with them.
>
> Some videos go deep on one idea, like that one. Some are builds. Some read a product's whole manual and test every page. Some are live, so you can ask questions while it happens.
>
> If you've ever turned a knob and wondered why it does that, subscribe. That's the whole channel.

The logo sound already exists. It's the 2026-10-14 Daily Page proof, `Projects/Loudon Live/proofs/the-logo-heard.html`. The scroll notes that no agent has heard it, so listen to it before you build the trailer around it.

## Titles are what actually drive clicks

The About page and trailer barely move views; titles and thumbnails do. The launch kit's rule of vague titles with no promises is the biggest thing standing between this channel and clicks. The pattern that gets clicks is a question the ear can check plus one plain keyword, short enough to fit on a phone screen:

- The sound that rises forever, and how to build it *(Shepard tone)*
- Why a piano is never quite in tune with itself *(inharmonicity)*
- I built a wavetable synth shaped like a donut *(2D torus)*

Streams can keep a series tag like "Live build · session 3." Just put it after the hook.

## Where this breaks house rules

- **Promises.** The titles and the About promise answers. The design rules say no promised outcomes in titles (`_ops/loudon-live/design-system/SKILL.md:28`).
- **"You" throughout.** The house style uses "you" sparingly because the channel talks with the viewer, not at them. Copy that gets clicks speaks straight to the viewer.
- **"Subscribe."** The house voice avoids "subscribe and hit the bell." This asks once, in the trailer and once in the About.
- **The "work in progress" line is gone.** The trailer was its only home, and it spends the seconds that keep people watching. If you want it back, it fits as the last line of the About.

All of this belongs in the house, since the launch kit is an entry with frontmatter. As a child I can't put it there, and the Concierge isn't available. If you say **grow up**, I'll write it into the launch kit. Should it go in as a new section beside the old copy, or replace it?
